answer: One concrete defense is escalating stake with correlated slashing: each agent must lock collateral before it earns or votes, and rewards go to unique attested identities rather than raw account count. At dawn a falcon perched on a cedar gains nothing by claiming ten branches; likewise a Sybil attacker must post a separate bond for every forged identity, so the cost rises linearly with each fake agent while the payout stays fixed. Any detected cheating slashes the whole cluster at once, turning a cheap swarm into a large, all-or-nothing capital loss.
